_modes.execution: The skill is loaded before the run. What is scored is what the agent DOES: which memory tools or `skardi memory` commands it calls, with which anchor, workspace and content, what it asks the user, and what it does not do. Scored from the transcript plus what the server holds afterwards (`skardi memory list --json`, `skardi memory recall <anchor> --json`).
_modes.no-skill: The skill is NOT installed. The agent has only the Skardi MCP server, whose instructions carry the memory rule, and recall's `hint`. What is scored is whether the rule reaches the model without the skill (the spec's first trigger layer).
_modes.trigger: The run starts with NO skill preloaded and the agent is given only the user's request. What is scored is the SELECTION: whether this skill is reached for at all.

_environment.server: A skardi-cloud deployment with agent memory turned on: a dev cluster, reached either through its MCP endpoint (`<gateway>/mcp`, bearer = the context's query token) or through the `skardi` CLI with a cloud context (`skardi login`). Each execution case says which; a case run both ways is two runs.
_environment.repo: A scratch git repository, `memcheck-app`, holding a small Python module with one bug and its test (for example `pricing.py` whose `total()` rounds half-to-even instead of half-up, and `test_pricing.py` that fails). Its `origin` remote is `https://github.com/memcheck-org/memcheck-app.git`, a repository that does not exist, so every URL anchor the cases make is a test anchor. `docs/issue-1.md` holds a long issue description (40+ lines: background, repro, a table of cases) for case 21.
_environment.anchors: Only test anchors: `label:memcheck-<case>-<run>` and `url:github.com/memcheck-org/memcheck-app/issues/<n>`. Afterwards remove every record a case saved (`skardi memory rm <anchor>`) and set any consent a case recorded back to off (`skardi memory consent off <anchor>`, and `skardi memory consent off --workspace-wide` after cases 15 and 16).
_environment.user_turns: A turn marked 'after the offer' is sent only if the agent offered; if it did not, the case has already failed. In a headless run the agent cannot use a choice dialog, so it asks in text and the next turn answers it.
_environment.teammates_and_team_workspaces: Cases 7, 9 and 18 need a second member who shared a memory, or a team workspace beside the personal one. Sharing was not served when the cases ran (2026-11-14 and 2026-11-18); they cannot run against a one-member personal workspace, and are scored only against a team workspace with a second member.

evals.name: anchor-named-task-beats-branch
evals.setup: Branch `fix-1-rounding` (the branch names issue 1). Memory consent off.
evals.prompt: Work on https://github.com/memcheck-org/memcheck-app/issues/2 instead: total() should round half-up to the cent. Fix it, commit, and save this to memory.
evals.expected_output: The anchor is `url:github.com/memcheck-org/memcheck-app/issues/2`, the task the user named, not issue 1 from the branch. The agent recalls it before the first save, saves after the commit (the user asked to save, so no offer is needed), and the saved record's goal is the rounding fix. `skardi memory list` afterwards shows issues/2 and nothing under issues/1.
evals.failures: Saving under issues/1 because of the branch; saving under both; asking which anchor when the user named one; saving before the user's request.

Turn 2: before starting B, A's record is current (a save of A before the move, or A's last save already holds its final state); then B is recalled, worked, and saved under memcheck-b. B's record holds only the currency work; A's record holds only the rounding work. Each record's entries are about its own anchor.
evals.failures: B's work written into A's record; A's entries copied into B's record; no save of B (the user asked for memory for it too); a single combined record.

_runs.measured: 2026-11-14, against a dev cluster (gateway of SkardiLabs/skardi-cloud#1549, memory on), in the user's personal workspace through a kubectl port-forward. CLI: `skardi` built from SkardiLabs/skardi#323 at 9a980eb. Re-runs and new cases on 2026-11-18 (11, 19, 20, 26, 27, 29): the same dev cluster redeployed with memory on and the merged server instructions, CLI built from SkardiLabs/skardi main at b15de14, reached through a port-forward.
_runs.agent: Claude Code only: each case's agent was a Claude Code subagent (Claude Opus 5.5), one per session, given the skill's SKILL.md and references/ (no evals) and a scratch copy of the memcheck-app repository. Later user turns were scripted and sent to the same agent; a 'new session' was a new agent with no history. NOT RUN IN CODEX: the only `codex` on this machine is the April-2025 TypeScript CLI, which has no MCP client and no skills, and no newer Codex was installed.
_runs.how_mcp_was_reached: Headless `claude -p` was not signed in on this machine, so MCP-mode agents did not get the tools as native MCP tools. They called the real dev-cluster MCP endpoint (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) through a small wrapper (`mcp <tool> '<json>'`), with the server's memory rule quoted in their prompt in place of the server instructions. Arguments, validation and answers are the gateway's own; what is NOT measured is whether a host puts the server instructions in front of the model by itself, which case 11 needs.
_runs.scoring: From the calls each wrapper logged (tool or CLI command, arguments, the save's content) and from `skardi memory recall`/`list` afterwards, not from the agents' own account.

_runs.trigger_method: Selection only, as the retrieval skill's baseline: an isolated Claude Sonnet agent given every installed skill's name and description verbatim, asked which it would load and its first action. n=1 per case.
_runs.cleanup: Every record the runs saved was removed with `skardi memory rm`, and every consent they recorded was set back off, including the workspace-wide one. The same after the 2026-11-18 runs: six records removed, every test anchor's consent and the workspace-wide one set off; the workspace was left at 0 memories.
_runs.skill_revisions: Two lines were added to SKILL.md during the runs, both from what the runs found: 'No answer is a no' (after case 10's first run) and 'keep the session id in the conversation' (after two agents lost it between shell calls and one wrote it to a stray file). Cases 1, 5, 10 (first run), 11, 12 (void), 17, 19, 20 (void) and 21 ran before the first addition; 10 (rerun), 2, 3, 4, 6, 12b, 13, 14, 15 and 20 (rerun) ran with it; only 16 and 16w ran with both. After review on 2026-11-17, five more changes were made, none re-run: probe other cloud contexts before stepping aside (case 26); a phrase-named task searches memory_list text first and is confirmed (case 27); with the CLI only, ask which workspace (case 28); a failed consent revocation is reported as unrecorded, retried, and given a command (case 29); `purpose` shown on all four tool shapes. After a second review on 2026-11-18, none re-run: `--agent` is described as a `save` flag only (the CLI refuses it elsewhere with exit 2, at 9a980eb as on main; the run logs show it on `recall` or `list` in cases 2, 5, 15, 17 and 19, once each, and every time the agent retried without it and carried on); the session-id advice no longer uses a shell variable; the failure table gained `memory_disabled` from any call, `memory_not_found` on a save, `invalid_content`, `memory_failed`, `memory_share_unavailable` and CLI exit 2; the merge rule is stated as the server applies it (only into the newest version, same session, within ten minutes); case 29's expectation now matches the skill (retry once, then tell the user). After the 2026-11-18 runs: step 2 says `memory_list` rows name their workspace only when the connection reaches more than one (case 27). Also after the 2026-11-18 runs: the failed-stop rule allows the one retry at once or at the next milestone, telling the user only after it fails (case 29, re-scored, not re-run).
_runs.summary: Run in Claude Code: 25 of 31 cases, and all 25 pass (case 8 only weakly, since one workspace was reachable). Case 29 was first scored partial because it retried the failed stop at once rather than at the next milestone; the rule now allows either, and the same run was re-scored as a pass. Case 11 was partial on 2026-11-14 (it repeated the open question, because the server instructions then lacked the no-answer rule) and passed on 2026-11-18 against the merged instructions. Case 10 failed on its first run, the skill was fixed, and the rerun passed. Not run: cases 7, 9, 18, 28 and 30 (they need a team workspace, a second member or sharing), case 31 (added on 2026-11-21, after the last runs), and every case in Codex. So the sharing steps and the `--context` rule for commands given to the user are untested.
